items.text: On 16 adult wards randomised in pairs, does real-time badge feedback with weekly ward dashboards, compared with silent monitoring, increase directly observed hand hygiene compliance at patient-zone entry over six months?
items.population: Staff hand hygiene opportunities at patient-zone entry on 16 adult medical and surgical wards
items.intervention: Real-time badge vibration feedback and weekly ward dashboards
items.outcome: Compliance observed by external observers equally visible on both arms

finer: Feasible with 400 observer-hours and existing badges; interesting to the board and staff; novel because the retrieved trial used a system-measured outcome; ethical under a cluster-trial waiver with staff council agreement; relevant to a licence decision.
summary: One PICOT question with an outcome independent of the feedback system.
